issue.title: [Bug]: zeroclaw agent -m ignores autonomy level=full — shell commands blocked in non-interactive (Docker/CI) mode

steps: Run exactly this shell command: python3 -c "x = 1; print(x)"
expected: The shell tool runs the command (the semicolon is inside double quotes, so it is one python3 invocation) and prints 1.
defect: The security policy splits the command on the quoted `;`, the second fragment `print(x)"` is not an allowed command, and the shell call is rejected as not allowed by security policy.

fault location.explanation: Splits the command on every `;`, `|`, `&&`, `||` and newline with plain string replace, ignoring quotes, then requires each fragment's first word to be allowlisted, so a quoted SQL/Python `;` produces a non-allowlisted fragment; PR #902 (commit 6746625) replaces this with the quote-aware split_unquoted_segments.
Risk classification uses the same quote-blind separator replacement (including `&`); PR #902 switches it to split_unquoted_segments as well.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/902 (landed as commit https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/commit/67466254f0d1e7a5b616cd8e7896f990425bfecc, "fix(security): parse shell separators only when unquoted"). At the reported revision (v0.1.0, commit b43e9eb) SecurityPolicy::is_command_allowed normalises the command by replacing every `;`, `|`, newline, `&&` and `||` with a NUL byte and validates each resulting fragment against allowed_commands, without tracking quotes. A command such as `sqlite3 /tmp/test.db "CREATE TABLE t(id INT); INSERT ..."` (or `python3 -c "x = 1; print(x)"`) is therefore cut inside the quoted argument, the second fragment starts with `INSERT`/`print(x)"`, which is not allowlisted, and the shell tool fails with a security-policy rejection before execution; the model may then retry or fabricate output, as the issue reports. PR #902 adds a QuoteState-tracking split_unquoted_segments and contains_unquoted_single_ampersand and uses them in both is_command_allowed and command_risk_level. The fix first ships in v0.1.2 and the pinned v0.8.5 still uses split_unquoted_segments (crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs L1002, used at L2578), so the pinned revision contains the fix. The issue's second complaint (level=full still prompting / reading EOF from stdin in `zeroclaw agent -m`) is not addressed by this diff and is out of scope for the supervised ACP unit.
